ignore.reason: `recipesOf` renders the catalog and pattern view into copyable imports and usage skeletons. The business rules it appears to hold belong to the catalog it reads; the function itself decides only how to spell an import.

plumb is the deterministic single-file linter: its rules are written once and applied everywhere, and its rule-authoring shapes are its own concern. joggle asks whether two things are the same and whether a thing fits THIS repository; plumb's rule internals are not that question, and the root lint already scopes plumb out. Judging them produced 82 `rule-judgment` readings about plumb's own rule metadata, 4 `object-shape` readings about its metadata literals, 3 `duplicate-meaning` and 2 `compose-types` readings within its own rule internals — none of them about this repository.

treadle is an application imported as its own tree -- its own Biome gate and two compiler settings -- not one of the seam packages the architecture law describes. Its loop-engine internals (trackers, rules, budgets, receipts) would be judged against a vocabulary they do not use, which is the same reason plumb's rule internals are scoped out. Converting it to the house rulebook is a recorded MIGRATION item, not a silent exception.

`DuplicateCandidate` and joggle's `ScoredPair` are two packages' independent declarations of a scored pair. They cannot compose: the dependency law is that `protocol` depends on nothing, so it cannot import a type from `joggle`. The shared shape IS the seam — they agree on bytes, not on code.

`decodeCatalogComponent` and `decodeMenuEntry` decode two different records that happen to share the field-by-field decode idiom (isRecord, then `str` per field). Factoring the idiom out would couple the two records' decoders to each other, which is the opposite of what each decoder exists for. The repetition is the boundary pattern, not a copy.

`RuleSetting.onUnavailable` is the RESOLVED setting and may be `count`; a rule's own declaration (`PlannedRule.onUnavailable`) is `report` | `propagate`, because a rule saying `count` would be meaningless. The two are different levels of one policy and the widening is deliberate, not a drift.

`dirOf` is a five-line path scan that exists in cutlist and joggle because the tools never import each other; sharing it would turn the format seam into a runtime dependency. The two also answer differently at the top level (`""` here, `"."` in joggle), so a common helper would change one caller's meaning.
`baseOf` is a filename scan used to read a declaration's name; joggle's copy serves bundle naming. Same seam as `dirOf`: two engines that agree on bytes, not code.

The other side of the `dirOf`/`baseOf` pair: joggle and cutlist each carry the five-line path scan because the tools never import each other. The ignore is recorded on both files so the finding cannot move with whichever side the detector names.

`lines` is a five-line split-and-trim that exists in jig-cli and joggle because the harness never links an engine. They also answer differently on purpose: joggle splits on CRLF, jig-cli on LF. Same seam as `dirOf`/`baseOf` — two deployables that agree on bytes, not code.

The other side of the `lines` pair: jig-cli and joggle each carry the helper because the tools never import each other. Recorded on both files so the finding cannot move with whichever side the detector names.

The same seam as the duplicate-implementation entry above: `dirOf` exists in cutlist and joggle because the tools never import each other, so the detector naming it a second time under the reversal rule is the same fact, not a new one.
`baseOf` is the other half of the `dirOf`/path-scan pair: two engines that agree on bytes, not code.

jig and joggle each decode a package manifest, a tsconfig and their own cache because the harness never links an engine. The seam is the reason the two implementations may diverge; a shared decoder would be the runtime dependency the workspace forbids.

`CachedFacts` and `CachedIndex` share the four envelope fields because that IS the cache format both files write; their entries differ (a position and a resolved type versus a line, a name and a fact). The rule read the envelope as one declaration written twice. Factoring a generic would make the version, tool and manifest fields' meaning depend on a type parameter for no reader's benefit.

`DuplicateCandidate` and joggle's `UnitPair` are two packages' independent declarations of a scored pair, and protocol cannot import joggle. The shared shape is the seam; the existing compose-types entry above records the same fact.

`RepoProfile.packageManager` is the RESOLVED manager, a closed union; `PackageManifest.packageManager` is the raw field as it appears in package.json, and that name is the JSON key the decoder reads. Two levels of one fact — the same shape joggle's own `onUnavailable` entry records.

The reader is identical in cutlist, jig-cli and joggle because the tools never import each other: a shared module would be the runtime dependency the seam forbids. `Packaged` and `readVersion` are the same five lines in each deployable, and each reads ITS OWN manifest — the file that differs between them.

The other face of the reversal entry above: cutlist, jig-cli and joggle each read their own package.json because a shared reader would be the runtime dependency the seam forbids. The five lines are identical on purpose; what differs is the manifest they read.
Cutlist is a read-only projection: the repair for an invariant it reports is a developer edit or a `cutlist build`, not a runtime reconciler. The detector is the whole contract.
The staleness and drift checks are read-only reports. Repair belongs to `cutlist build`, which writes the catalog; adding a reconciler here would make the checker a writer.

`isTestPath` and `isTid` are already `Predicate.Predicate<string>`; the shared element is that type, which both packages already have. A runtime regex-predicate helper in `protocol` would add runtime to the package chartered as no-runtime.

`Census` and `Loaded` share field names but not meanings: `entries` is a count in the census and a map in the load. Extending one from the other would make the count a map; the repetition is the two contracts, not a copy.
The baseline's repair path is `jig baseline`, which writes the ledger. `diffBaseline` and `ratchetViolations` are the read-only detectors; a reconciler here would collapse the writer and the check.
`nearestDuplicate` is an advisory candidate finder. The repair is a developer's edit, named in the report; a runtime reconciler would decide a design question for them.

`CutlistOutput`'s fields are independent optional destinations: absence means 'not written', not a missing deviation field. Sharing a base with the vocabulary would tie an output path to an ownership setting.
IgnoreRule is authored config: its authority is git and it has no instant; the missing runtime `suppressed` report is tracked as its own change, not disguised as a field here.
The three branches choose a sentence, not a list format; memberList is the one formatter. The rule reads the repeated template as a second path.

evidence.repository: The dependency law from README.md and pnpm-workspace.yaml, written a second time where the import rule can read it: protocol depends on nothing, each engine depends on protocol and never on a sibling, and the harness depends on protocol and drives the engines as processes — it never links them. `packages/plumb` and `packages/joggle` are named here and both now exist, so the law was declared once and the move had only to satisfy it. The layer order is the part to re-derive: a linear order says 'may not import upward', and the harness's rule is the stronger 'may not import a sibling engine at all'. A `presets` entry stood here naming `@autotelic/joggle/presets/structure`; that preset exists only on joggle's unimported line, so it went with it and the explicit rule list below is the whole intent. The other shipped preset, `presets/composition`, is deliberately not used: its own header calls it somebody's architecture — opted into, not defaulted on.
